paragraphs.text: SSH command plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): manage hosts and credentials in Settings, then run co
mmands on one or many remote Linux/macOS hosts from the chat. TOFU host keys, dangerous-command appr
oval, persistent shells and SFTP.
English · 简体中文
Remote Bash is an SSH plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Register a few remote Linux / macOS hosts i
n Settings, then let the agent run commands on one host or a whole group in a single call.
Passwords, private keys and sudo passwords are stored in the local DSH credential store; the model o
nly sees whether a credential is configured. Host keys are recorded on first connect and rejected if
they change later. Dangerous commands go through an approval prompt, and a persistent session keeps
`cd` / `export` state between calls.
## Settings page
The plugin adds a **Remote Bash** section to Settings, with three tabs: hosts, known hosts and persi
stent sessions. Each host row can test the connection, edit credentials and show its recorded finger
sessions. Each host row can test the connection, edit credentials and show its recorded fingerprint.
*Layout illustration; colors follow your DSH theme.*

Requires DSH 0.2.x (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`) and Node 20+. The plugin depends on `ssh2`, which npm in
stalls during setup; no local `ssh` client or `sshpass` is needed.

| `always` | Ask

## Authentication and security
The full path of one call:
**Credentials.** Passwords, key passphrases and sudo passwords go into the `records` space of the DS
H credential store (`remote-bash/refs/<UUID>`; legacy `remote-bash/<hostId>` records remain readable
) with file mode 0600. Reads and writes happen only inside the Host process, and the API returns jus
t "configured / not configured". One boundary is worth stating: like the DSH credential store itself
, any process running as the same OS user (including the agent's shell tools) can read that file in
principle. That is a file-permission limit; the plugin cannot isolate further.
**Host keys.** On first connect the SHA256 fingerprint of the host key is written to `known_hosts.js
on`, and every later connection is checked against it. A mismatch rejects the connection and leaves
the new fingerprint pending in Settings; approving it affects that one host. This protects against m
an-in-the-middle and also catches a replaced machine.
**Dangerous commands.** Commands matching a built-in rule (`rm -rf` on dangerous paths, `mkfs`, `dd`
to a device, shutdown, stopping critical services, account changes, firewall flushes, overwriting s
ystem config, etc.) or carrying `sudo` go through `ctx.approval`. The rules are regex heuristics: th
ey can miss and they can false-positive, and a false positive costs one extra confirmation. Add `ext
raDangerousPatterns`, or use `approvalMode: always`. If the approval service is unavailable, the com
erns`, or use `approvalMode: always`. If the approval service is unavailable, the command is denied.
**sudo passwords** are sent through SSH stdin only after a per-command authentication prompt. Genera
ted commands contain no password, and the target command has separate, empty stdin. Cached authentic
ation and NOPASSWD send no password. Sudo runs a non-login Bash shell, so it does not automatically
source login profiles.
**Commands and output** become part of the current session record; that is how DSH works, so keep se
crets out of commands. The plugin does not collect data and does not talk to any network address oth
er than the hosts you configure.
Report security issues privately as described in SECURITY.en.md.
## Architecture
The Host process opens SSH connections itself, using the pure-JS `ssh2` package. That avoids dependi
ng on the local ssh version and needs no askpass helper for password auth; SSH agent forwarding is n
ot implemented. The browser half only handles the Settings page and talks to the Host over a DSH-aut
henticated local RPC (`/api/remote-bash/rpc`).
Persistent sessions are `bash -s` on the same SSH channel, without a PTY. `cd` and `export` survive
between calls; terminal programs such as vim or top do not work. Commands have empty stdin by defaul
t; use explicit pipes or redirection when input is needed. Cancelling or timing out an active sessio
n command closes that session; a later call can create a new one. Busy sessions are not evicted as i
dle. Cancelling a queued call does not cancel another active call.
## Known limitations

- Targets must be Linux / macOS (POSIX shell).
- Persistent sessions have no PTY, so interactive TUI

programs do not work.
- Dangerous-command rules are heuristics: they accept false positives and may

miss things.
- Local paths are resolved relative to the Host process working directory; absolute pa

ths are safer.
- The Settings section appears after a page refresh following the first install.
- No
t supported yet: SSH agent, bastion hosts / ProxyJump, Windows targets.
